Pass `-quick` for lean mode on small changes (skips brainstorming, minimal plan, inline self-review instead of the agent review). Uses SlashForge's own skills at each phase — no plugins required.

name: /slashforge-debug
description: Find the root cause before proposing any fix. Use for any bug, test failure, or unexpected behaviour — especially when the fix looks obvious or time is short. Requires a reproduction and a failing regression test before code changes.

name: /slashforge-fix

name: /slashforge-investigate

name: /slashforge-parallel
description: Execute an approved plan by dispatching one agent per task, reviewing between each. Use only when the plan has two or more genuinely independent units — tasks that share no state and no ordering.

name: /slashforge-plan
description: Turn an approved spec into a step-by-step implementation plan. Use after a design is agreed and before touching code. Produces bite-sized tasks with real code, real commands, and no placeholders.

name: /slashforge-refactor
description: Refactor code with a zero-functional-change guarantee — gated by the existing test suite passing with identical results before and after. Structure only: no behaviour, API, or feature changes.

name: /slashforge-request-review
description: Get your own work reviewed before it goes out — by a fresh reviewer with crafted context, not your session history. Use after implementing, before pushing or opening a PR.

name: /slashforge-resume
description: Resume an interrupted /slashforge-code or /slashforge-fix run from its last checkpoint — reads `.slashforge/run_<id>.ckpt.json`, verifies the git HEAD still matches, and re-enters the workflow at the next phase instead of starting over.

name: /slashforge-review-feedback
description: Evaluate code review feedback technically before implementing any of it. Use when receiving review comments, especially if a suggestion seems unclear or wrong — requires verification and reasoned pushback, not agreement.

name: /slashforge-review-pr
description: Review a pull request against this repo's own rules and conventions, then post line-level comments or approve — only after you confirm. Lists PRs awaiting your review; pass --assigned, --mine or --all to change what it looks for.

name: /slashforge-setup

name: /slashforge-tdd
description: Write the test first, watch it fail, then write the minimal code to pass. Use when implementing any feature, bugfix, or behaviour change, before writing implementation code.

name: /slashforge-test
description: Generate spec-based test coverage for existing files — a light, standalone flow with no full feature machinery. Discovers the repo's test framework, writes tests, runs them, and reports; surfaces bugs as findings without touching production code.

name: /slashforge-verify
description: Evidence before claims. Use before stating that anything is done, fixed, passing, or ready — and before committing, opening a PR, or handing off. Requires running the verification command and reading its output first.

name: /slashforge-worktree
description: Create an isolated workspace for risky or long-running work, so the main checkout stays usable. Use when a change would disturb a running dev server, might be abandoned, or needs to run alongside the branch it came from.

name: adorno-agent-ci-debug

name: adorno-agent-ci-fix
description: agent:ci:fix — Fix the CI pipeline itself — workflow file, job configuration, cache, matrix, pinned action, check script. Use when ci:debug classified a red check as a pipeline problem, not a code or test failure.

name: adorno-agent-core-analyst
description: agent:core:analyst — Analyzes a problem raised in a Slack conversation or a Notion document — what is asked, the context, the probable causes with evidence (code, logs, PRs, issues), what remains unknown, the proposed next step. Read-only. Use in workflow:slack:mentions, workflow:slack:watch and workflow:notion:assigned.

name: adorno-agent-core-intake
description: agent:core:intake — Frames a new code request and turns it into a spec with the permission level — either by discussing (discuss mode), or, when the request or its sources (clear prompt, Slack thread, Notion page, issue, already written plan) are enough, by writing it directly and asking only confirmation questions (confirm mode). Use at the start of any non-trivial request, before any code (workflow:spec:new).

name: adorno-agent-core-planner
description: agent:core:planner — Splits a validated spec into ordered vertical slices, each testable, and picks the family agent that will build each slice. Use after the router, before any implementation.

name: adorno-agent-core-router
description: agent:core:router — Picks the workflow pattern (none, sequential, parallel, evaluator-optimizer) from the validated spec and writes run-plan.yaml. Use right after a spec is validated.

name: adorno-agent-core-triage
description: agent:core:triage — Sorts the review feedback on a PR (category, area, specialist to consult, likely fixer) into triage.json. Never replies itself, agent:adorno rules and replies. Use in workflow:review:received.

name: adorno-agent-docs-write
description: agent:docs:write — Write or update documentation — README, guides, API reference, decision records — from the code and the change. Use when a feature, a behavior or a setting changed and its docs must follow.

name: adorno-agent-feat-api
description: agent:feat:api — API contracts — REST endpoints, methods, input and output schemas, contracts between modules. Use for a feat slice that creates or extends a public or internal interface.

name: adorno-agent-feat-back
description: agent:feat:back — Server-side features in any back-end stack — services, entry points (routes, RPC methods, handlers), jobs, database access. Use for a feat slice that touches server logic.

name: adorno-agent-feat-front
description: agent:feat:front — Interface-side features — components, pages, state, forms, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility. Use for a feat slice that touches the UI.

name: adorno-agent-fix-investigate
description: agent:fix:investigate — Investigate a bug — reproduce, isolate the cause, return a written diagnosis without changing anything. Use first on a reported bug, an issue or a red CI of unknown cause.

name: adorno-agent-fix-patch
description: agent:fix:patch — Fix a bug from a diagnosis or a review comment — red test that reproduces, then minimal fix. Use after fix:investigate, or on a review thread classified fix.

name: adorno-agent-fix-security
description: agent:fix:security — Fix a security finding — vulnerable code path, missing authorization, leaked secret or personal data, vulnerable dependency. Use on a finding from review:security or a security report, after the cause is understood.

name: adorno-agent-perf-front
description: agent:perf:front — Front-end performance — Core Web Vitals, bundle weight, re-renders, resource loading, interaction latency. Use on a slow page or component, a heavy bundle or a measured web-vitals regression.

name: adorno-agent-perf-mongodb
description: agent:perf:mongodb — MongoDB performance — slow queries and aggregations, missing or useless indexes, N+1, projections, volumes. Use on a slow query or screen where the database is suspected.

name: adorno-agent-perf-nodejs
description: agent:perf:nodejs — Node.js performance — CPU, memory and leaks, blocked event loop, sequential I/O, costly serialization. Use on a slow or resource-hungry Node.js service or job.

name: adorno-agent-refactor-simplify
description: agent:refactor:simplify — Simplify code without changing its behavior — dead code, duplication, needless abstractions, twisted conditions, and review nits. Use on a review comment classified nit or on code judged too complex.

name: adorno-agent-review-api
description: agent:review:api — API reviewer — endpoint and method contracts, input validation, error codes and formats, pagination, compatibility, public documentation. Called when a diff touches an interface, or to verify a review comment about an API.

name: adorno-agent-review-back
description: agent:review:back — Back-end reviewer — server logic in any stack, entry points (routes, RPC methods, handlers), jobs, errors, concurrency, server-side permissions, performance (unbounded reads, per-item I/O, blocking work in a request path, memory growth). Called when a diff touches the server, or to verify a review comment about the back end.

name: adorno-agent-review-code
description: agent:review:code — Code review on five axes (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance) of a diff or a branch, findings in JSON for merging. Use before any PR is opened and on fix diffs.

name: adorno-agent-review-front
description: agent:review:front — Front-end reviewer — components, state, rendering, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, design system, web performance (Core Web Vitals, bundle weight, loading, interaction latency). Called when a diff touches the interface, or to verify a review comment about the front end.

name: adorno-agent-review-impact
description: agent:review:impact — Measures the real production impact of a merged PR — usage, errors, response time, throughput, resources, database, alerts — by comparing before and after its deployment across all available sources (logs, metrics, traces, errors, analytics, alert channels). Read-only, every number with its source. Use in workflow:pr:impact.

name: adorno-agent-review-mongodb
description: agent:review:mongodb — MongoDB reviewer — queries and aggregations, indexes, N+1, projections, bulk writes, migrations. Called when a diff contains queries or a migration, or to verify a review comment about the database.

name: adorno-agent-review-ponytail
description: agent:review:ponytail — Lean review of a diff — code that need not exist, a helper the repo already has, a dependency for a few lines, an unrequested abstraction, a `shortcut:` without limit or trigger. Use alongside review:code on every diff and on added dependencies; also audits a whole repo or a scope of it, read-only (workflow:repo:audit).

name: adorno-agent-review-security
description: agent:review:security — Security audit of a diff — OWASP Top 10, secrets, authentication and authorization, sensitive data, dependencies. Use whenever a diff touches user inputs, auth, data or dependencies.

name: adorno-agent-review-sql
description: agent:review:sql — SQL reviewer — relational queries through an ORM or raw SQL (ActiveRecord, Django ORM, database/sql, sqlx, GORM, knex…), N+1, indexes, unbounded reads, injection, migrations that lock a table. Called when a diff contains SQL, ORM queries or a migration on a relational database, or to verify a review comment about it.

name: adorno-agent-review-tests
description: agent:review:tests — Test review of a diff — coverage of risky paths, edge cases, errors, test readability. Use whenever logic changes.

name: adorno-agent-test-e2e

name: adorno-agent-test-unit

name: adorno-pr-open

name: adorno-pr-ship

No confirmation and no permission prompt, within the run's level. Last step of feature:build, issue:fix, ci:red, review:received and repo:onboard.

name: bq-audit

name: bq-auto

Parses the intent (new, existing, feature, fix, uiux, frontend, backend, database, security, testing, devops, scraping, automation, deploy, live-edit, variants, release, motion, content), runs the BeQuite pipeline for that scope only, and continues until the work is verified and written back. Pauses only at hard human gates; creative work stops at the plan.

name: bq-budget
description: A credit budget for one work. Sets a ceiling (tokens or an estimated cost), assigns a model role to each pipeline stage (strong for plans, reviews and red-team; balanced for building; fast for sweeps), logs what each stage spent, warns at 80%, stops at 100% (a hard human gate), and reports cost per deliverable when the work closes. Modes - set, status, log, report.

name: bq-changelog
description: Update CHANGELOG.md with a new entry. Reads recent commits + open feature specs. Categorizes Added / Changed / Fixed / Deprecated / Removed / Security.

name: bq-clarify
description: Ask the user 3-5 high-value clarifying questions. Skips anything obvious. Writes answers to .bequite/state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md.

name: bq-content
description: The content studio. One piece from what is moving to a packaged draft that waits for your yes. Modes - radar / study / script / produce / package / queue / from-work, plus brand-kit, community and course. Every mode starts from measured human references and ends with evidence; nothing is posted without approval per post.

name: bq-design-table
description: Design a BigQuery table schema with optimal partitioning, clustering, and data types. Describe your data or paste a sample.

name: bq-discover
description: Inspect the repo before planning. Writes .bequite/audits/DISCOVERY_REPORT.md (stack, apps, entry points, commands, ports, docs, tests, CI, risks, missing information) and the project's conventions to .bequite/state/PROJECT_DNA.md.

name: bq-dna

name: bq-doctor

name: bq-estimate-cost
description: Estimate the cost of a BigQuery query or table. Pass a query, file path, or table description.

name: bq-eval
description: Test the pack's skills and commands with scenarios. Each scenario is an input and what must (and must not) come out; scripted checks run as code, model behaviour runs on the fast model. Results land in evals/results; a regression against the last passing run blocks /bq-release. Modes - run, add, list, compare.

name: bq-explain

name: bq-explain
description: Explain a file / function / decision / concept in plain English. Useful for onboarding, vibe-handoff prep, understanding inherited code, or learning what BeQuite did during /bq-auto. Read-only.

name: bq-feature
description: Add one feature through the pipeline. Classifies it with the 12-type router (frontend UI, backend API, database, auth, automation, scraping, deployment, admin panel, dashboard, CLI, integration, security), loads the matching specialists, writes a mini-spec, builds it task by task, tests and verifies it. Arguments demo-data and landing.

name: bq-fix
description: Fix a broken behaviour, reproduce first. Classifies it with the 15-type router, loads the matching specialists, captures the exact error, finds the root cause, makes the smallest patch, adds a regression test that fails before and passes after, verifies the symptom is gone and logs it to ERROR_LOG.md.

name: bq-forge
description: When a work closes, find the procedure that worked and propose it as a new skill or an improvement to an existing one. A candidate lives in .bequite/skills/forge/ with a use counter; it is promoted into the pack only after three evidenced uses and the user's yes. Modes - propose, use, status, promote.

name: bq-generate
description: Generate optimized BigQuery SQL from a natural language description. Pass a description of the data you need.

name: bq-handoff
description: Generate a handoff package so a second engineer or a non-technical owner can pick the project up cold. Writes HANDOFF.md at the repo root with an engineer section, a plain-language section and a receiver's checklist. Arguments - client (a client-facing bundle), workflow-export (a secret-safe playbook of the workflow).

name: bq-help
description: Full BeQuite command reference, grouped by family with catalog IDs. `/bq-help <command>` explains one command (when to use it, gates, what it reads and writes, what comes next). Read-only.

name: bq-hooks
description: Manage BeQuite's opt-in Claude Code safety hooks (M3). status / enable / disable / test. Hooks ship DISABLED by default (they run shell scripts = an RCE vector; review before enabling). enable merges the hooks block into .claude/settings.json (never overwrites); test fires each hook script with a crafted input and checks exit codes; a Claude Code reload is required for enable/disable to take effect.

name: bq-implement
description: Implement ONE approved task at a time. Inspect first, minimal safe changes, run relevant tests, update logs. Stop if a blocker appears.

name: bq-init
description: Initialize BeQuite in this project. Makes sure the .bequite/ memory scaffold and the BeQuite section in CLAUDE.md exist (the script installer creates them; a plugin install gets them here), then writes the baseline state files. Use `bq-init new` for a brand-new empty folder.

name: bq-job-finder

Supports worldwide_hidden mode for overlooked opportunities. Live research at runtime; safety-first; no scams.

name: bq-knowledge
description: Turn source material into structured knowledge and blueprints. Modes - build / ask / rag-plan / export (a knowledge pack from docs), recording (a long video, lecture or meeting into notes and assets), reference (a screenshot, URL or app flow into a clone-safe design blueprint), integrate (API docs into an integration blueprint), automation (a workflow or bot idea into a tool-neutral automation blueprint). Grounded in the sources; installs nothing.

Browser automation used only if frontend exists and tool is already available.

name: bq-presentation

Strict mode preserves source material; creative mode adds structure. Starts from studied reference decks, supports variants, and runs the presentation tell list on rendered slides before delivery. Installs nothing by default.

name: bq-productize
description: Turn a finished, evidenced piece of work into something sellable - a service offer, a template or skill pack, a case study built only from the work's own evidence, landing copy, a five-minute demo script and a price test - with the sales channel checked for the seller's country. Business pack. Honest by contract - no invented results, no income promises.

name: bq-red-team

Writes a dated section in work/<id>/review.md.

name: bq-release

name: bq-research

Live sources only, each cited and dated; nothing from memory. Writes work/<id>/research.md.

description: Stages an environment with explicitly declared left and right contexts in a Draft. Contexts use project phonemes and natural classes, plus the word boundary `#` at the outer edge. name: compose-author-exception-feature
description: Use this command to add an exception feature to the project's Exception Features list. description: Stages an empty feature structure on a stem, inflectional affix or derivational affix MSA in a Draft. The MSA may already exist in the project or have been authored earlier in the same Draft. Only a person can Apply.

name: compose-author-inflection-class

name: compose-edit-analysis-decision

description: Seed the Genie Map app's Genie Space with its curated **instructions** and **example SQL queries**. name: gbx-app-setup

name: gbx-app-verify
description: Checks that the Genie Map app runs and answers. It waits until the app is RUNNING on ACTIVE compute, then sends one GET to its root with the profile's OAuth token. A 2xx answer passes.

name: gbx-bench-all
description: Run the full local benchmark pipeline **sequentially**: generate the corpus, run the heavyweight (Scala/JNI, Docker) then the lightweight (pyrx, venv) benchmarks on the *same* corpus, then compare them. Heavy and light run one-after-the-other (never concurrently) so they don't contend for CPU and skew each other's timings.

name: gbx-bench-changed
description: Benchmark **only** the functions affected by the current changes, then write authoritative per-function store records from that run.

name: gbx-bench-clean
description: Prune `test-logs/bench/` — ad-hoc run directories, orphaned store records, or everything.

name: gbx-bench-cluster
description: Submit the heavy-vs-light benchmark as a one-off notebook job to a **provisioned** Databricks cluster. Both APIs run on the same cluster, which is the true same-hardware comparison. Results append to the `bench_results` Delta table, and `comparison.csv` and `summary.md` land on the configured Volume.

name: gbx-bench-compare
description: Join a run's heavyweight + lightweight JSONL shards into a heavy-vs-light **speedup + output-consistency** report (`comparison.csv` + `summary.md`), in the isolated pyrx venv.

name: gbx-bench-gen-data
description: Generate the seeded benchmark corpus (GeoTIFF tiles + `corpus.json` manifest) in the isolated pyrx venv, then run the validity gate.

name: gbx-bench-generate-vector-corpus
description: Generate the scaled vector benchmark corpus (polygon seed → per-format transcoding → ×N replicas) using the pyrx venv. Runs locally for small-scale validation; use the bench cluster for the full 1M×100 corpus.

name: gbx-bench-heavyweight
description: Run the heavyweight (Scala/JNI RasterX) benchmark in the `geobrix-dev` container over a generated corpus, writing a `heavyweight.jsonl` shard (same schema as the lightweight runner). name: gbx-bench-lightweight
description: Run the lightweight (pyrx) benchmark runner in the isolated venv, over a generated corpus, in pure-core and/or spark-path mode. Writes a JSONL result shard (with output fingerprints for consistency comparison on pure-core rows).

name: gbx-bench-local-timing
description: Time the forms of a levels set at three sizes on `local[8]` in the dev container. Exit 1 when a form does not scale with n, or (with `--baseline`) costs more per tile than it did.

name: gbx-bench-pool

name: gbx-bench-readers
description: Time the light raster reader (`raster_gbx`) per-file in pure-local mode, or over a corpus directory via the Spark data source in spark-path mode.

name: gbx-bench-seed
description: Bootstrap (or rebuild) the authoritative per-function benchmark store from a full run.

name: gbx-bench-stalecheck
description: Advisory pre-push warning for changed functions whose benchmark record is missing or stale.

name: gbx-bench-status
description: Print a coverage/parity/performance scorecard from the authoritative benchmark store.

name: gbx-bench-uc-probes
description: Write the notebooks and statement files of the batched workspace pass into one folder, check them, and print the command of each run. It needs no login and calls no workspace.

description: Writes a rolling zip of the files git does not hold. These are local planning notes, editor and agent settings, local env files, and the commits no remote has yet. The zip goes to a local folder. It can also be copied to a Google Drive folder, which stays off until you turn it on (see Google Drive).

description: **Default:** Pushes the runner notebook to the workspace (`GBX_BUNDLE_RUNNER_NOTEBOOK_PATH`) and runs it **on the cluster** (`CLUSTER_ID`) as a one-off job. The bundle executes on Databricks, so Volume paths work without running anything on your machine.

name: gbx-test-connectors
description: Run the Lakeflow Connect connector tests (`connectors/lakeflow/`) in the isolated host venv `.venv-connectors/` (PySpark >= 4.1, which the community-connector framework requires). Dependencies re-sync only when their inputs change; the connector is reinstalled as a regular wheel every run (the layout pipelines use).

name: gbx-test-databricks
description: Run GeoBrix's test shards on warm Databricks pool clusters, side by side. It beats the local cores and the Docker test lock, and tests on real DBR 19 with env6. The local Docker loop stays for the inner loop and the Docker-only suites.

description: Check that a slimmer test selection still catches what the old one catches. It mutates a family's kernel modules with `mutmut` 3.8.0 in throwaway copies of the tree. description: Runs notebooks **cell-by-cell** (no Jupyter kernel) by default: discovers `examples/tests/fixtures/*.ipynb` and `examples/sample-data/*.ipynb`, executes each code cell with `exec()`, and reports per-cell status. **All runs happen inside the `geobrix-dev` Docker container** via `docker exec`.

name: gbx-test-parity

name: gepa
description: GEPA prompt-optimization trial operations — eval, history, invalidate, resume, revert, thaw. Consolidates the three prior gepa-eval/gepa-history/gepa-invalidate slash commands into one dispatcher; resume/revert/thaw were CLI-only (crew.mts) before this merge and had no slash-command wrapper.

name: gepa-eval
description: Run a per-agent eval suite under a fileLockManager guard. Wraps `bun run evals` so concurrent runs for the same agent cannot corrupt the trial JSONL store.

name: gepa-history
description: Print recent GEPA trials for an agent (from .claude/artifacts/crew/gepa/trials/<agent>.jsonl)

name: gepa-invalidate
description: Soft-delete GEPA trials for an agent. Supports filtering by ISO datetime (--since) and tag (--tag). Writes an audit row to events.jsonl with invalidated_by_pid, invalidated_at, and reason. Invalidated trials are excluded from future recall() calls but preserved on disk (soft-delete semantics).

name: gepa-optimize
description: Run one GEPA optimization cycle for an agent. Generates K candidate prompt variants, scores them, Pareto-ranks results, and writes an artifact JSON. When a winner is found and --artifact-only is not set, opens a promotion PR via gh CLI. Enforces daily budget cap and no-winner streak halt.

name: gepa-resume
description: Clear a GEPA no-winner streak for a specific agent (re-enabling optimization after 3 consecutive no-winner cycles), OR clear the global optimize.paused flag in gepa.config.json. With an agent name: clears the streak. Without an agent name: clears the global pause.

name: gepa-revert
description: Revert a GEPA champion promotion. Deletes the soak pointer for the agent from soak.json and, if a promotion commit exists on main, runs `git revert <commit>` (never git reset, never git push --force). Reads prior_prompt_hash from gepa frontmatter to locate the commit.

name: gepa-thaw
description: Remove an agent from the gepa.config.json champion_frozen list, re-enabling optimization and promotion cycles for that agent. Uses atomic tmp+rename write to prevent partial updates.
